_what_this_is: Rates INTO the reporting currency: reporting_value = transaction_value * rate.
So GBP 1.3229 means one pound is 1.3229 US dollars.
A currency that is not listed here is NOT assumed to be 1.0. Its money columns are
blanked and the run reports how many lines that cost, because a missing rate that
silently becomes 1.0 turns INR 126,550 into USD 126,550 and nothing downstream can
Where an export carries its own exchange-rate column, that rate wins over this file.
It is the rate the transaction actually settled at; this table is the fallback.
_effective_dating: Each entry applies from its effective_from date until the next entry for that
currency. Purchase history spans years, so one flat rate over the whole window
would render a currency move as a procurement trend. A line raised before the
earliest entry takes that earliest entry — approximate, but better than unvalued.
Add a new dated entry each planning cycle rather than editing the last one, so a
re-run of an old extract still reproduces the numbers it originally reported.
_maintenance: The seed rates below were read off the PL30 July 2026 open-PO export, which carries
both the transaction value and SAP's own converted value — their ratio is the rate
SAP booked. They are a starting point, not a treasury feed: replace them with the
planning rates your finance team publishes, and date each revision.
_placeholder_note: CNY and SGD below are marked placeholder: true. They are stand-ins so a run
completes and the magnitudes are right — they are NOT measured or published
rates, and every run that uses one says so. Derive the real rate the way the
seeds above were derived: take an export line's transaction value and SAP's own
converted value, and use their ratio. Then drop the placeholder flag.
